narratives.narrative: Psa 5:1 opens the psalm not with a formed petition but with a groan the psalmist asks God to weigh: sense (101, id 7691496) is 'groaning God is asked to consider', typed as affect (102, id 7691497). The bearer (105, id 7691499) is the psalmist himself, and the operation (106, id 7691500) is the self bringing a groaning too deep for words and asking God to give heed to it - pre-verbal distress. Target (107, id 7691501) folds back onto the groaning itself: the inner sound is what is offered up. Coupling (112, id 7691503) binds it to the petition 'consider-my-groaning', so the groan is not vented into the air but directed Godward. Source (103) is present:false - no origin outside the self is named; the groan simply rises from the interior. Seat (104, id 7691498) is 'none': this is not organ-located, not lodged in a heart or bones, but a whole-self state - confirmed by locus (116, id 7691504) 'internal:ib-state'. Manner (108) is 'none', so the groaning carries no qualifying style; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111) and prohibition (113) are all present:false - the reader logged no measured degree, no narrowing specifier, no recorded downstream effect and nothing forbidden. The discovery (114, id 7691505) names the finding: the interior's first offering is not eloquence but a groan asking to be understood beneath the words. Role (115, id 7691506) is characteristic - a genuine movement of the inner life, God its arena and hearer, not its subject.
narratives.story: The psalm begins not with polished words but with a groan. Before he can shape a single request, the man is simply making a wordless sound of distress, and his first act is to ask God to pay attention to that sound rather than to any argument. The groan rises straight out of him - nothing outside is blamed for it, and it is not felt in any one part of the body but is the whole self aching. He does not throw it out at random; he turns it deliberately toward God and asks to be understood beneath his words. Nothing here rates how loud or how strong it is, and no result is recorded - the point is only that the deepest part of a person can speak to God in a groan before it can speak in sentences.

narratives.narrative: Psa 6:6 records weeping as nightly flood: sense (101, id 7691788) 'nightly weeping floods the bed', typed affect (102, id 7691789). Bearer (105, id 7691791) is the psalmist; the operation (106, id 7691792) is that every night the self floods its bed and drenches its couch with tears - grief overflowing in the dark hours. Target (107, id 7691793) is the weeping itself, and coupling (112, id 7691795) 'flood-the-bed' welds the tears to the physical bed they soak. Source (103) is present:false - no external cause is fixed to the tears here; they simply pour. Seat (104, id 7691790) is 'none' and locus (116, id 7691796) 'internal:ib-state': the weeping is a whole-self overflow, not lodged in an organ. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) all present:false - no degree scored, no specifier, no logged effect, nothing forbidden, though the drenched couch itself testifies to volume the schema does not quantify. The discovery (114, id 7691797) marks this reading as deliberately distinct from the weariness of the same verse: this is the active, measurable overflow of grief through the night, not the exhaustion that follows. Role (115, id 7691798) is characteristic. The inner-being process is grief made liquid and repetitive - a self that dissolves nightly, its bed the arena where sorrow is spent.
narratives.story: Every night the man cries until his bed is soaked and his couch is drenched. This is grief that has become physical - tears pouring out in the dark hours, night after night, until the bedding itself is wet through. Nothing outside is named as the cause; the weeping simply overflows from the whole of him, not from any single part. The account is careful to mark this off from mere tiredness: this is the active flood of sorrow, the visible measure of how much he is hurting. It does not put a number on the tears, but the drenched bed says enough - a person coming apart quietly, alone, every night.

narratives.narrative: Psa 12:5 gives a groan with power: sense (101, id 7693055) 'the needy groan', typed affect (102, id 7693056). Unusually for this family the bearer (105, id 7693058) is not the psalmist but 'the poor / needy' - a collective of the oppressed. The operation (106, id 7693059) is decisive: because the poor are plundered and the needy groan, God rises to act - the inarticulate groan that summons rescue. Target (107, id 7693060) is the groaning itself; coupling (112, id 7693062) 'needy-groan' binds the sound to the class that utters it. Source (103) present:false - the plundering is the narrated occasion but no separate source-row is fixed to the groan. Seat (104, id 7693057) 'none', locus (116, id 7693063) 'internal:ib-state': whole-self, not organ-bound. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false - no scored degree, no specifier, and, strikingly, no effect-row even though the verse states the effect (God arises): the schema leaves the consequence in the operation rather than the effect field. Discovery (114, id 7693064) states the finding: the interior of the crushed is a groan, and it is precisely this sound that moves God to rise. Role (115, id 7693065) characteristic. The inner-being movement here is a groan that is efficacious - grief so real it becomes a summons; God is the arena that answers it.
narratives.story: Here the groan belongs not to the singer but to the poor and the plundered - the people who have been robbed and have nothing left but the sound of their suffering. Their groan is not weak: it reaches God and moves him to stand up and act. It is a wordless cry, rising from the whole of crushed people, and it is exactly this sound that God answers. Nothing measures how loud it is, and the account keeps the rescue tied to the cry itself rather than treating it as a separate outcome. The lesson is stark and hopeful at once: the bare groan of the helpless is enough to make God rise.
narratives.variation_note: First of three readings of H0603:groan. Here the bearer is the oppressed poor collectively (not the psalmist), and the groan is efficacious - it summons God to arise and act. In Psa 79:11 (#2) and Psa 102:20 (#3) the bearer narrows to captive prisoners and the movement shifts from summoning God to being brought before / heard by God; the difference is a shift from a groan that moves God to rise, to a groan lifted as petition and then heard.

narratives.narrative: Psa 30:5 reads weeping not as an act in progress but as a settled insight about grief's shape: sense (101, id 7696890) 'weeping tarries the night, joy at morning'. Distinctively for a tears-word it is typed cognition (102, id 7696891), not affect - the tears are being thought about, not shed. Bearer (105, id 7696893) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7696894) is that the self reflects that God's anger is momentary but his favour lifelong, so weeping may tarry for the night but joy comes with the morning - a hard-won reading of grief's arc. Target (107, id 7696895) is that very 'grief's-arc'; coupling (112, id 7696897) 'weeping-to-joy' binds sorrow to its dawn resolution. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7696892) 'none'; locus (116, id 7696898) 'internal:ib-state' - a whole-self understanding, not organ-lodged. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false - no degree, no specifier, no logged effect, nothing forbidden. Discovery (114, id 7696899) names it: the interior learns that sorrow is temporary and joy is the sure dawn. Role (115, id 7696900) characteristic. The inner-being process is grief reframed by reflection - the self holding its own weeping at arm's length long enough to see it bounded by morning; God's anger and favour are the arena that gives the tears their measure.
narratives.story: Here weeping is not happening - it is being understood. The man has stepped back far enough to see the shape of his own sorrow: God's anger lasts only a moment, but his kindness lasts a lifetime, so tears may stay through the night, but joy arrives with the morning. This is grief turned into a hard-won piece of wisdom, a settled conviction that sorrow is temporary and gladness is the sure dawn. Nothing outside is blamed and no strength of feeling is measured; it is simply the whole self learning to trust the shape of its own pain. Weeping, seen this way, is bound to the morning that ends it.

narratives.narrative: Psa 32:4 reads 'heavy' as the felt weight of unrelieved guilt: sense (101, id 7697503) 'your hand was heavy on me', typed state (102, id 7697504). Bearer (105, id 7697506) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7697507) is that day and night God's hand was heavy on the self and its strength dried up as by summer heat - the felt pressure of conviction. Target (107, id 7697508) is 'conviction's-weight'; coupling (112, id 7697510) 'heavy-hand' binds the pressure to the divine hand that applies it. Source (103) present:false - though the verse names God's hand as the pressing agent, no separate source-row is recorded; the weight is registered as a state of the sufferer, not tagged to an origin. Seat (104, id 7697505) 'none', locus (116, id 7697511) 'internal:ib-state': the heaviness is whole-self, the strength dried out of the man rather than lodged in one organ. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false - no scored degree (though 'day and night' and 'dried up' imply severity the schema leaves unquantified), no specifier, no effect-row, nothing forbidden. Discovery (114, id 7697512) names it: the interior is pressed dry until it must confess. Role (115, id 7697513) characteristic. The inner-being movement is conviction felt as physical burden - grief not over loss but over unconfessed sin, the self crushed downward until release comes only through confession; God's disciplining hand is the arena.
narratives.story: This is the grief of a guilty conscience that will not let go. Day and night the man feels God's hand pressing down on him like a weight, and his strength drains away as if he were left out in the blazing heat of summer. It is not sorrow over a loss but the crushing pressure of sin he has not yet admitted - the whole of him wrung dry, not just some part. The account does not rate how bad it is, but 'day and night' and 'dried up' say plenty. He is pressed down until the only relief left is to confess, and God's heavy hand is what finally squeezes the truth out of him.

narratives.narrative: Psa 35:14 reads lament as grief borrowed for one's enemies: sense (101, id 7698376) 'I mourned for them as for kin', typed affect (102, id 7698377). Bearer (105, id 7698379) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7698380) is that the self went about as though grieving for a friend or brother, bowed in mourning as for its mother - identifying with the enemies' suffering. Target (107, id 7698381) is 'kinship-grief'; coupling (112, id 7698383) 'mourn-as-for-kin' binds his mourning to the closest family bonds. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7698378) 'none'; locus (116, id 7698384) 'internal:ib-state' - whole-self, not organ-bound. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false - no degree, no specifier, no logged effect, nothing forbidden. Discovery (114, id 7698385) marks it distinct from the fasting of the surrounding verses: this is the depth of felt grief, the interior mourning enemies as its closest family - later betrayed when at his stumbling they rejoiced. Role (115, id 7698386) characteristic. The uncomfortable finding, held without softening: a self that pours out real kin-grade grief over people who are its adversaries - genuine sorrow spent on the undeserving, the enemies the arena onto which the inner being lavishes a mother's mourning.
narratives.story: When his enemies were sick, the man grieved for them as if they were his own family - walking about in sorrow as though mourning a friend, a brother, even his own mother. This is real, deep grief, the kind reserved for the closest of kin, and he spent it on the very people who hated him. Nothing measures how strong it was; it simply came from the whole of him. The bitter twist, which the text does not hide, is that when he himself later stumbled, those same people gathered and rejoiced. He gave them a family's tears and got mockery in return.

narratives.narrative: Psa 38:8 gives a groan forced out by inner uproar: sense (101, id 7699582) 'I groan from the tumult of my heart', typed state (102, id 7699583). Bearer (105, id 7699585) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7699586) is that the self is feeble and crushed and groans because of the tumult of its heart - inner uproar breaking out as groaning. Target (107, id 7699587) is 'inner-tumult'; coupling (112, id 7699589) 'groan-heart-tumult' binds the sound to the churning heart that produces it. Source (103) present:false - the heart's tumult is named in the operation but not fixed as a separate source-row. Seat (104, id 7699584) 'none': though the verse names the heart as where the tumult lives, the reader logs no seat for the groan itself - the groan is whole-self, confirmed by locus (116, id 7699590) 'internal:ib-state'. Manner (108) 'none'; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false - no scored degree, no specifier, no effect-row, nothing forbidden. Discovery (114, id 7699591) names it: the heart in uproar forces itself out as a groan; the interior's turmoil is audible. Role (115, id 7699592) characteristic. The inner-being movement is turbulence made sound - a heart in commotion that cannot stay silent, the groan the pressure valve of a crushed and feeble self.
narratives.story: Worn down and crushed, the man groans - and the groan is pushed out by the churning inside him. His heart is in uproar, and that turmoil cannot stay quiet; it breaks out of him as a raw, involuntary sound. The groan comes from the whole of him, not from any single place, even though it is the heart's commotion driving it. Nothing rates how loud or how bad it is. It is simply the noise a person makes when the storm inside has nowhere else to go - inner turmoil turned audible.

narratives.narrative: Psa 42:3 reads tears as food: sense (101, id 7649612) 'tears / weeping (dimah)', typed status (102, id 7649613) - a standing condition, not an act. Bearer (105, id 7649615) is David. Strikingly, operation (106, id 7649616), target (107, id 7649617) and coupling (112, id 7649619) are all 'none' - the reader found no movement, no object, no pairing: the tears are not doing anything, they simply are, a settled state of weeping. What is present is manner (108, id 7649618): 'his food day and night' - the sole qualifier, tears so constant they replace bread. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7649614) 'none'; locus (116, id 7649620) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false - no scored degree, no specifier, no effect, nothing forbidden. Discovery (114, id 7649621) names it: weeping so constant it replaces bread, while the foes taunt 'Where is your God?'. Role (115, id 7649622) characteristic. The inner-being process here is grief that has stopped being an action and become a diet - the self sustained on its own tears; the triple 'none' of operation, target and coupling is itself the finding: this is not weeping toward anything but weeping as the very substance the self lives on, the enemies' taunt the arena that keeps the tears flowing.
narratives.story: For this man, tears have become his food, day and night. He is not crying about something in particular or crying to get anything - the weeping has stopped being an action and become his whole condition, as steady as meals. He lives on his tears the way another lives on bread. All the while, people around him keep jeering, 'Where is your God?' - and that taunt keeps the tears coming. There is no measure of it and no outcome named; there is only a person so soaked in grief that sorrow itself has become what feeds him.
narratives.variation_note: One of five readings of H1832:tear. Unique in that this passage records no movement, object or pairing - tears as a static condition (food day and night), not an action. Contrast Psa 56:8 (#2, tears treasured by God), Psa 80:5 (#3, corporate tears as bread/drink), Psa 116:8 (#4, tears God dries by deliverance) and Psa 126:5 (#5, tears that seed a harvest of joy). Here uniquely the grief goes nowhere and does nothing - pure sustained condition.

narratives.narrative: Psa 42:9 reads mourning as dark going-about under a felt divine forgetting: sense (101, id 7649735) 'mourn / go about darkly (qadar)', typed action (102, id 7649736) - here mourning is something done, a way of walking. Uniquely for this family a source (103, id 7649741) is recorded and span-resolved: 'the felt divine forgetting + enemy oppression (v9)'. Bearer (105, id 7649738) is David; operation (106, id 7649739) is simply 'mourn'; target (107, id 7649740) is 'none' - the mourning has no object, it is a state of blackened going-about, not grief toward a thing. Manner (108, id 7649742) 'because of the enemy's oppression' qualifies it; coupling (112, id 7649743) 'none'. Seat (104, id 7649737) 'none'; locus (116, id 7649744) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7649745) names it: the dark grief of feeling forgotten by God, its cause the felt divine forgetting and the foe's oppression. Role (115, id 7649746) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief as a darkened gait - the whole self going about in mourning-blackness because it feels God has forgotten it; God's felt absence and the enemy's pressure together are the arena, and the doubled source (divine forgetting plus oppression) is the finding.
narratives.story: This is grief you can see in the way a man walks - going about darkened, dressed in gloom, mourning not for any one loss but as a whole way of moving through his days. Two things drive it: the crushing feeling that God has forgotten him, and the constant pressure of enemies who oppress him. The mourning is not aimed at anything; it is simply the shadow he lives under. It fills the whole of him, and no measure is put on it. He is a person walking in black because he feels abandoned by the God he calls his rock.
narratives.variation_note: First of two nearly identical readings of H6937:mourn (the other is Psa 43:2). Both are dark going-about (qadar) driven by enemy oppression, but the recorded source differs: here (42:9) the cause is the felt divine FORGETTING ('Why have you forgotten me?'); in 43:2 it is the felt divine REJECTION ('Why have you cast me off?'). The shift from being forgotten to being actively rejected is an intensification of the same wound.

narratives.narrative: Psa 43:2 repeats the dark mourning of Psa 42:9 almost verbatim but under a sharper wound: sense (101, id 7649849) 'mourn / go about darkly (qadar)', typed action (102, id 7649850). Source (103, id 7649855), again recorded and span-resolved, is here 'the felt divine rejection + enemy oppression (v2)' - not forgetting but rejection. Bearer (105, id 7649852) is David; operation (106, id 7649853) 'mourn'; target (107, id 7649854) 'none' - objectless dark going-about; manner (108, id 7649856) 'because of the enemy's oppression'; coupling (112, id 7649857) 'none'. Seat (104, id 7649851) 'none'; locus (116, id 7649858) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7649859) names it: the dark grief of the seemingly-rejected, verbatim from Psa 42:9, its cause the felt divine rejection and the foe's oppression. Role (115, id 7649860) characteristic. The inner-being movement is identical in shape - the whole self walking in mourning-blackness - but the felt cause has hardened from being forgotten (42:9) to being cast off (43:2); God is the arena whose withdrawal is now experienced as active rejection rather than mere neglect.
narratives.story: Again a man walks about darkened with grief, exactly as in the psalm before - mourning as a whole way of moving, not sorrow over one thing. And again two forces press him down: the weight of enemies who oppress him, and the feeling that God has turned away. But the wound has sharpened. Before, it was the sense of being forgotten; now it is the sense of being cast off, actively rejected by the God he asks to defend him. The grief looks the same, but it comes from a colder place. He goes about in shadow because he feels not merely overlooked but pushed away.
narratives.variation_note: Second of two near-identical readings of H6937:mourn (the first is Psa 42:9). The recorded source is the point of difference: 42:9 gives felt divine FORGETTING; here 43:2 gives felt divine REJECTION. Same darkened mourning, same enemy oppression, but the felt cause has intensified from neglect to active rejection - the variation is the deepening of the wound between the twin psalms.

narratives.narrative: Psa 55:2 gives a wordless moan beneath the spoken complaint: sense (101, id 7653489) 'moan / be in commotion (hum - I moan)', typed action (102, id 7653490). Bearer (105, id 7653492) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7653493) 'moan / groan'. Target (107, id 7653494) and manner (108, id 7653495) are both 'none' - the moaning has no object and no qualifying style; it is bare tumult. Coupling (112, id 7653496), span-resolved, is 'paired with restlessness' - the moan travels with a body that cannot be still. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7653491) 'none'; locus (116, id 7653497) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7653498) names it: the wordless groaning of anguish, hum being the inarticulate sound of a heart in commotion, beneath the spoken complaint - distress that overflows speech. Role (115, id 7653499) characteristic. The inner-being movement is the layer below words - while the mouth utters complaint, the self also moans, a commotion that words cannot contain; the restlessness it is paired with shows the whole person, body and interior together, unable to settle.
narratives.story: Underneath his words there is a sound with no words in it. As the man pours out his complaint, he is also moaning - a low, restless noise of a heart in turmoil that spills past anything he can actually say. It is not aimed at anyone and has no particular shape; it is just raw distress. It comes with a body that cannot keep still, so the whole of him is stirred up at once. This is the part of grief that runs deeper than speech - the moan that escapes when words are not enough.

narratives.narrative: Psa 55:17 gives a moan carried within deliberate prayer: sense (101, id 7653822) 'moan / murmur (hamah - and moan)', typed action (102, id 7653823). Bearer (105, id 7653825) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7653826) 'moan / groan'. Target (107, id 7653827) 'none' and manner (108, id 7653828) 'none' - no object, no qualifying style. Coupling (112, id 7653829), span-resolved, is 'paired with the complaint' - the moan rides alongside the uttered complaint that the verse offers evening, morning and noon. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7653824) 'none'; locus (116, id 7653830) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7653831) names it: the groaning that accompanies the prayer, hamah the sound of the heart's tumult kept up before the God who hears. Role (115, id 7653832) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief folded into a discipline - the moan is not random venting but is sustained three times daily and directed to the God who is expected to hear; the tumult of the heart becomes part of a rhythm of appeal, God the arena that receives it.
narratives.story: Three times a day - evening, morning, and noon - the man pours out his complaint to God, and folded into that prayer is a moan. It is a wordless groan, the sound of a heart in turmoil, and it is not thrown out at random: it is kept up steadily as part of his regular crying out to God. He has no polished words for it and no particular style; it is simply the turmoil inside, offered again and again. What makes this different is the discipline of it - grief brought back to God on a schedule, in confidence that God hears.
narratives.variation_note: One of two readings of H1993:moan (hamah). Here (Psa 55:17) the moan is twinned with the deliberate, thrice-daily complaint offered before the God who hears - grief as sustained, directed petition. In Psa 77:3 (#2) the same word is triggered by REMEMBERING God in the dark, producing distress rather than comfort. The difference: in 55:17 the moan is confident, rhythmic appeal; in 77:3 remembering God deepens the groan toward near-despair.

narratives.narrative: Psa 56:8 reads tears God treasures: sense (101, id 7654326) 'tears (dimah - put my tears in your bottle)', typed status (102, id 7654327). Uniquely among the tears-readings a source (103, id 7654334) is recorded and span-resolved: 'God puts them in his bottle, counts them (v8)' - the tears' origin is folded into God's own gathering of them. Bearer (105, id 7654329) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7654330) 'wept / shed'; target (107, id 7654331) 'none'. Manner (108, id 7654332) 'kept by God in his bottle / book' - the qualifier is not how they were shed but how they are stored. Coupling (112, id 7654333), span-resolved, 'paired with the restless tossings' - the tears travel with the sleepless turning the verse also records. Seat (104, id 7654328) 'none'; locus (116, id 7654335) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7654336) names it: the weeping God treasures, gathered as precious and recorded - grief not wasted but kept, the tenderest image of divine care in the psalm. Role (115, id 7654337) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief received and valued from outside the self - the tears are not merely shed but collected and counted by God; the target is 'none' because the tears do not aim, they are aimed at by God, who is the arena that treasures them.
narratives.story: The man asks God to catch his tears in a bottle and to write them down in his book - and he believes God actually does. His weeping is not wasted or ignored; every tear is gathered up and counted as precious, kept safe by God himself. The tears come from his sleepless, restless nights of tossing and turning, but the striking thing is not how he sheds them - it is how they are stored. This is the tenderest picture of care in the whole psalm: grief that no one else sees, treasured by God as if each drop mattered.
narratives.variation_note: One of five readings of H1832:tear. Unique in that a cause is recorded - God himself gathering, bottling and counting the tears - making the grief something received and treasured from outside the self. Contrast Psa 42:3 (#1, tears as static food), Psa 80:5 (#3, corporate tears as bread), Psa 116:8 (#4, tears God dries), Psa 126:5 (#5, tears that seed joy). Here uniquely the tears are precious to God and preserved rather than merely endured.

narratives.narrative: Psa 64:3 reads bitterness as a weapon in the wicked's mouth: sense (101, id 7656703) 'bitter (mar - aim bitter words like arrows)', typed status (102, id 7656704). Emphatically, the bearer (105, id 7656706) is 'the wicked', not the psalmist - the dark interior read on its own terms. This is the one reading in the family with a seat (104, id 7656705): 'the tongue' - the bitterness is organ-located, lodged in the instrument of speech. Operation (106, id 7656707) is 'aim (like arrows)'; target (107, id 7656708) 'the blameless'; manner (108, id 7656709) 'like arrows, tongues whetted like swords'. Coupling (112, id 7656710), span-resolved, 'the venom of the secret plots' binds the bitter words to hidden conspiracy. Source (103) present:false; locus (116, id 7656711) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7656712) names it: the venomous speech that is the enemies' weapon, malice loaded and aimed, shot from ambush at the blameless. Role (115, id 7656713) characteristic. Held without valence bias, this is the descent read as fully as any ascent: the inner life of the malicious, whose bitterness is not passive suffering but an interior sharpened into a weapon - seated in the tongue, aimed from concealment at the innocent; the blameless are the arena the wicked's bitterness targets.
narratives.story: This bitterness does not belong to the sufferer - it belongs to wicked men, and it is a weapon. They sharpen their tongues like swords and load their bitter words like arrows, taking aim from hiding at people who have done nothing wrong. The venom sits in the tongue itself, the tool they use to wound, and it works hand in hand with their secret plots. This is not grief that hurts inside; it is malice pointed outward, cruelty shaped into speech and fired from ambush. Read plainly, it shows the inside of cruel people: their bitterness is a loaded, aimed thing, targeted at the innocent.

narratives.narrative: Psa 69:10 reads weeping as devotion turned to reproach: sense (101, id 7660075) 'weep (bakah - when I wept and humbled my soul with fasting)', typed action (102, id 7660076). Bearer (105, id 7660078) is the psalmist. This reading carries a seat (104, id 7660077): 'the soul' - the weeping is lodged in the nephesh humbled by fasting. Operation (106, id 7660079) is 'weep and humble the soul (with fasting)'; target (107, id 7660080) 'before God'; manner (108, id 7660081) 'with fasting'. Coupling (112, id 7660082), span-resolved, 'the mourning that became his reproach'. Source (103) present:false; intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Locus (116, id 7660083) is 'external:god' - rare in this family: the weeping is oriented outward toward God, not held as a private inner state. Discovery (114, id 7660084) names it: piety itself turned into an occasion for mockery, his very humbling before God used against him. Role (115, id 7660085) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief as worship betrayed - the self weeps and fasts as genuine devotion directed at God (locus external:god), yet that very act, seated in the humbled soul, becomes the reproach the scoffers throw back; God is the arena the tears are offered to, the world the arena that mocks them.
narratives.story: When the man wept and went without food to humble himself before God, it was true devotion - grief poured out in worship, his very soul brought low as an offering. But his piety backfired in the eyes of others: the scoffers took his weeping and fasting and turned it into a joke, a byword to sneer at. The tears were aimed at God, sincerely; the mockery came from people who twisted his sincerity against him. This is the pain of having your deepest act of humility used to shame you - grief offered up to God, thrown back as an insult by the crowd.
narratives.variation_note: One of two readings of H1058:wept (bakah). Here (Psa 69:10) the weeping is personal devotion - weeping and fasting lodged in the humbled soul, directed toward God, which is then twisted into reproach. In Psa 137:1 (#2) the weeping is corporate exiles' grief triggered by the memory of Zion (held as inner state). The difference: 69:10 is private worship betrayed into mockery; 137:1 is communal sorrow loosed by remembrance of a lost home.

narratives.narrative: Psa 77:3 gives a moan that remembering God makes worse: sense (101, id 7663445) 'moan / murmur (hamah - I moan)', typed action (102, id 7663446). Bearer (105, id 7663448) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7663449) 'moan / groan'; target (107, id 7663450) 'none'. Both manner (108, id 7663451) 'in remembrance of God' and coupling (112, id 7663452) 'paired with remembering God' are span-resolved and point the same way: the moan is triggered and accompanied by the act of remembering God. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7663447) 'none'; locus (116, id 7663453) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7663454) names it: the audible groan of the troubled heart, hamah the low murmur of distress as the mind dwells on God in the dark. Role (115, id 7663455) characteristic. The uncomfortable finding, not filtered: here remembering God does not console but deepens the groan - the very act that should steady the self instead loosens a moan. The inner-being movement is grief intensified by devotion's own memory; God is the arena, but recalling him in the dark produces tumult rather than peace, the moan the measure of a faith that finds no comfort in remembrance.
narratives.story: In the dark, the man remembers God - and instead of comforting him, it makes him moan. Thinking about God, which should steady a troubled heart, only loosens a low groan of distress. The moan has no particular target; it is simply the sound of a mind dwelling on God and finding no relief. The text does not soften this: remembering God here brings turmoil, not peace. It is an honest picture of a faith in crisis, where the very thought of God deepens the ache rather than easing it.
narratives.variation_note: Second reading of H1993:moan (hamah). In Psa 55:17 (#1) the moan is folded into confident, thrice-daily prayer before the God who hears. Here (Psa 77:3) the same word is triggered by remembering God in the dark and produces distress rather than comfort. The variation is a reversal of effect: remembrance that should console instead deepens the groan - devotion intensifying grief.

narratives.narrative: Psa 77:10 reads grief as the hinge of the whole psalm: sense (101, id 7663555) 'grief / my appeal (challothi - this is my grief)', typed state (102, id 7663556). Bearer (105, id 7663558) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7663559) is 'name the grief / resolve to appeal' - the self naming its wound. Target (107, id 7663560) is 'the changed right hand of the Most High'; manner (108, id 7663561) 'the turning-point of the psalm'. Coupling (112, id 7663562), span-resolved, 'paired with the resolve to remember God's deeds (v11)'. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7663557) 'none'; locus (116, id 7663563) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7663564) names it: the hinge of the psalm, where the sufferer names his wound and, in naming it, pivots from questioning God's silence toward remembering his deeds - grief spoken becomes the doorway to hope. Role (115, id 7663565) characteristic. The inner-being movement is distinctive within this family: grief not merely felt or vented but named and owned, and in the naming turned into a hinge - the self says 'this is my grief' and thereby pivots from the changed right hand of God toward the recollection of his deeds; God is the arena, and the act of articulating the wound is what opens the turn from despair.
narratives.story: Here grief becomes a turning point. Instead of only feeling his pain, the man names it out loud - 'this is my grief: that God's strong hand seems to have changed toward me.' And in the very act of naming the wound, something shifts. Saying plainly what hurts becomes the doorway out: from here he turns from brooding on God's silence to deliberately calling to mind the things God has done. This is grief owned and spoken rather than merely endured, and the speaking is what lets hope back in. Putting the pain into words is the hinge the whole psalm swings on.

narratives.narrative: Psa 78:40 reads grief inflicted upon God: sense (101, id 7664296) 'grieve / pain (atsab)', typed action (102, id 7664297). Distinctively, the bearer (105, id 7664299) is 'they' - the rebellious wilderness generation - and the target (107, id 7664301) is 'to God': the grief does not belong to the sufferer here but is the pain the people cause God. Operation (106, id 7664300) is 'grieve / cause pain'; coupling (112, id 7664303) 'paired with the rebelling'. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7664298) 'none'; manner (108, id 7664302) 'none'. Locus (116, id 7664304) is 'external:god' - the grief is located in God, its object outside the human self. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7664305) names it: the pain their rebellion inflicted on God himself. Role (115, id 7664306) characteristic. This inverts the family's usual direction: grief here is not the inner being suffering but the inner being of the people acting to wound another - God is not the arena that hears grief but the one grieved. The finding, held plainly, is that human rebellion is read as a grief-causing operation directed at God; the seat 'none' and manner 'none' leave it unqualified, a bare inflicting of pain upward.
narratives.story: This grief is not the singer's - it is the grief the people caused God. Again and again in the wilderness they rebelled, and their rebellion actually wounded God, causing him pain. The direction is reversed from the usual picture: instead of a person hurting and crying to God, here people are the ones inflicting the hurt, and God is the one grieved. Nothing qualifies how or how much; it is simply stated that their defiance pained him. It is a sobering thought - that stubborn rebellion is not just disobedience but something that genuinely grieves the God against whom it is aimed.

narratives.narrative: Psa 79:11 gives the groan of captives lifted to God: sense (101, id 7665186) 'groans (anaqah)', typed state (102, id 7665187). Bearer (105, id 7665189) is 'the prisoners' - a corporate, national body of captives. Operation (106, id 7665190) is 'groan in captivity'; target (107, id 7665191) 'before God'; coupling (112, id 7665193) 'paired with the plea to preserve those doomed to die'. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7665188) 'none'; manner (108, id 7665192) 'none'; locus (116, id 7665194) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7665195) names it: the anguished sighing of the captives, the sound of suffering lifted to God as its own petition. Role (115, id 7665196) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief as petition without words - the groan of the imprisoned is itself brought 'before God', functioning as a prayer; here the psalm asks God to let the groan come up before him, so the groaning is directed and consciously offered, coupled to a plea for the condemned. God is the arena the captives' groan is set before.
narratives.story: The prayer here asks God to let the groans of the prisoners rise up before him. These are captives - a suffering people locked away - and their groaning is treated as a prayer in its own right, lifted deliberately into God's presence. It goes hand in hand with a plea that God would spare those under sentence of death. The groan is not measured or described in any special way; it is simply the raw sound of imprisoned suffering, set before God so that he will hear it and act. Their sighing becomes their petition.
narratives.variation_note: Second of three readings of H0603:groan. The bearer here is captive prisoners (corporate/national), and the groan is deliberately set 'before God' as a petition, twinned with a plea for the condemned. Contrast Psa 12:5 (#1), where the groan of the poor summons God to arise, and Psa 102:20 (#3), where the near-identical prisoners' groan is what God stoops to hear, leading to release. The movement here is the groan being lifted up as petition, rather than moving God to rise (#1) or being heard from above (#3).

narratives.narrative: Psa 80:5 reads tears as the nation's food and drink: sense (101, id 7665409) 'tears (dimah)', typed state (102, id 7665410). Bearer (105, id 7665412) is 'the people' - corporate Israel, not an individual. Operation (106, id 7665413) is 'weep'; target (107, id 7665414) 'in grief'; coupling (112, id 7665416) 'paired with the tears given as drink'. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7665411) 'none'; manner (108, id 7665415) 'none'; locus (116, id 7665417) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7665418) names it: the people's weeping become their very sustenance - God has fed them with the bread of tears, grief so constant it is eaten as bread. Role (115, id 7665419) characteristic. The inner-being movement is corporate grief made diet, and pointedly God is named as the one who feeds them tears - the sorrow is not merely endured but administered from above; the people are the whole-self bearer, weeping in grief while God gives them tears both to eat (bread) and to drink. God is the arena that both causes and could relieve the weeping.
narratives.story: This is a whole nation weeping, not just one person. Their tears have become their food and their drink - God has fed them with the bread of tears and made them drink tears by the bowlful. Grief has become so constant that it is what they live on, morning and night. And the text names God himself as the one who has served them this diet of sorrow. It is corporate anguish, a people so soaked in weeping that tears are their bread and their water - and the God they cry to is the one who has given it to them.
narratives.variation_note: One of five readings of H1832:tear and the corporate parallel to the personal ones. The bearer is the whole people (Israel), and God is explicitly the one who feeds them tears as bread and drink. Contrast the individual Psa 42:3 (#1, tears as one man's food), Psa 56:8 (#2, tears treasured by God), Psa 116:8 (#4, tears God dries), Psa 126:5 (#5, tears that seed joy). Here uniquely the weeping is national and administered by God as sustenance - grief given from above rather than merely suffered.

narratives.narrative: Psa 88:9 reads sorrow that dims the eyes: sense (101, id 7667723) 'sorrow (oni)', typed state (102, id 7667724). Bearer (105, id 7667726) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7667727) 'suffer sorrow'; target (107, id 7667728) 'daily' - the affliction is registered as unrelenting, day after day. Coupling (112, id 7667730) 'paired with the dimming eye' binds the sorrow to the physical wasting of the eyes it causes. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7667725) 'none'; manner (108, id 7667729) 'none'; locus (116, id 7667731) 'internal:ib-state'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7667732) names it: the affliction that dims the eyes, unrelenting grief. Role (115, id 7667733) characteristic. In the darkest psalm of the Psalter this is grief with no resolution offered - sorrow suffered daily until the eye itself grows dim, and the schema logs no effect-row for relief because the psalm offers none. The inner-being movement is passive, chronic affliction: the whole self bearing sorrow that wears the body down; God is the arena addressed, but here uniquely no turn toward hope follows.
narratives.story: Day after day this man simply suffers. His sorrow never lifts - it is constant, wearing him down until even his eyes grow weak and dim from the weight of it. Unlike most of these psalms, no relief comes and no bright turn arrives; the grief just goes on. It is the kind of ongoing affliction that quietly ruins the body over time, and it fills the whole of him. He still cries out to God, but here, in the bleakest of these songs, the sorrow is left standing with no answer - an honest picture of grief that does not resolve.

narratives.narrative: Psa 102:5 reads groaning worn into the body: sense (101, id 7672286) 'groaning (anachah)', typed action (102, id 7672287). Bearer (105, id 7672289) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7672290) 'groan aloud'; target (107, id 7672291) 'in affliction'. In this passage the coupling and locus fields carry transposed-looking values that must be reported as recorded: coupling (112, id 7672293) holds 'internal:ib-state' - marking the groan as bound to the inner state - while locus (116, id 7672294) holds 'paired with the wasted flesh', tying the groaning to the body it consumes. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7672288) 'none'; manner (108, id 7672292) 'none'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7672295) names it: the constant groaning of the sufferer, grief worn into the body - 'because of my loud groaning my bones cling to my flesh'. Role (115, id 7672296) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief so sustained it has physical cost: the groan is loud and continual, and its consequence is a wasted frame, bones clinging to flesh. The whole self groans in affliction until the body itself is diminished; God, addressed throughout the psalm, is the arena the loud groaning is spent before.
narratives.story: The man's groaning has become so loud and so constant that it is wasting his body away - he is so worn down that his bones seem to cling to his skin. This is grief that never stops long enough to let him recover; it groans on and on in his misery until his frame is thin and consumed. The groan is bound up with his whole inner state and shows itself in his shrunken body. There is no measure put on it and no relief noted here - just a suffering man whose endless groaning is literally eating him away.

narratives.narrative: Psa 102:9 reads tears drunk with the cup: sense (101, id 7672319) 'tears (beki)', typed state (102, id 7672320). Bearer (105, id 7672322) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7672323) 'weep'; target (107, id 7672324) 'mingling tears with drink'. As at Psa 102:5, the coupling and locus fields carry transposed-looking values reported as recorded: coupling (112, id 7672326) holds 'internal:ib-state', and locus (116, id 7672327) holds 'paired with eating ashes' - the weeping is tied to the ashes eaten as bread in the same verse. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7672321) 'none'; manner (108, id 7672325) 'none'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7672328) names it: the weeping that fills the sufferer's cup, grief drunk with the water. Role (115, id 7672329) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief taken in with the body's intake - the self eats ashes like bread and mingles its tears with its drink, so sorrow is not only shed but consumed; weeping saturates even the act of drinking. The whole self is steeped in mourning; God, the psalm's addressee, is the arena the tear-soaked lament is set before.
narratives.story: This man's food is ashes and his drink is mixed with his own tears. He weeps so much that his crying spills into his cup - when he drinks, he is swallowing his own tears along with the water. Grief has soaked into the most basic acts of eating and drinking, so that mourning is not only something he does but something he takes in. Nothing measures how much, and no relief is noted here. It is a picture of a person so steeped in sorrow that even his meals taste of it.

narratives.narrative: Psa 102:20 gives the prisoners' groan that God stoops to hear: sense (101, id 7672418) 'groans (enqah)', typed action (102, id 7672419). Bearer (105, id 7672421) is 'the prisoners'; operation (106, id 7672422) 'groan'; target (107, id 7672423) 'before God'. As elsewhere in Psa 102 the coupling and locus carry transposed-looking values reported as recorded: coupling (112, id 7672425) holds 'internal:ib-state', locus (116, id 7672426) holds 'paired with being set free' - the groan is tied to the liberation it leads to. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7672420) 'none'; manner (108, id 7672424) 'none'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7672427) names it: the sighing of the captives that God stoops to hear - 'to hear the groans of the prisoners... to set free those doomed to die'. Role (115, id 7672428) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief that reaches its answer: the captives' groan is heard from above, and it is paired with their release. God is the arena that looks down and hears; here, unlike the summoning groan of Psa 12:5 or the merely-lifted groan of Psa 79:11, the emphasis falls on the divine hearing and the freedom it brings.
narratives.story: God looks down from heaven and hears the groaning of prisoners - the sighing of people locked away and under sentence of death. Their groan is not wasted: it reaches God, who bends down to listen, and it is bound up with their being set free. The sound is simply the raw distress of captives, but it is heard, and hearing it God moves to release those condemned to die. Here the groan is not left hanging; it is answered from above, and freedom follows.
narratives.variation_note: Third of three readings of H0603:groan. The bearer, captive prisoners, matches Psa 79:11 (#2), but the movement differs: in 79:11 the groan is lifted UP before God as petition, while here (102:20) the emphasis is on God HEARING it from above and setting the doomed free - grief that reaches its answer. Both differ from Psa 12:5 (#1), where the groan of the poor summons God to arise. The variation traces a groan's arc: it moves God to rise (#1), is offered up as petition (#2), and is heard from heaven and answered with release (#3).

narratives.narrative: Psa 106:33 reads bitterness inflicted on Moses: sense (101, id 7675086) 'bitter (marah)', typed state (102, id 7675087). Bearer (105, id 7675089) is 'Moses' - not the psalmist and not the wicked, but the servant embittered by the people. Operation (106, id 7675090) 'be embittered'; target (107, id 7675091) 'in spirit'. The coupling and locus carry transposed-looking values reported as recorded: coupling (112, id 7675093) holds 'internal:ib-state', locus (116, id 7675094) holds 'paired with the spirit and rash words' - the embittering is tied to the spirit it soured and the rash words it produced. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7675088) 'none'; manner (108, id 7675092) 'none'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7675095) names it: the embittering of Moses, provocation working inward. Role (115, id 7675096) characteristic. The inner-being movement is bitterness as something done to a person from outside - the people provoked Moses until his spirit was made bitter, and that soured spirit issued in rash words. The finding, held plainly, is a chain: external provocation to embittered spirit to unguarded speech; the people are the arena that embitters, Moses the inner being whose spirit is turned bitter and betrayed into rashness.
narratives.story: The people wore Moses down until they made his spirit bitter. This is bitterness done to a person - the constant provoking of the crowd souring the inside of a good man until something curdled in him. And that embittered spirit had a consequence: it spilled out in rash, unguarded words. The chain is simple and human: they goaded him, his spirit turned bitter, and then he spoke without thinking. Even a leader like Moses could be pushed to the point where the bitterness others stirred up in him broke out of his mouth.

narratives.narrative: Psa 107:39 reads sorrow among the humbled: sense (101, id 7676236) 'sorrow (yagon)', typed state (102, id 7676237). Bearer (105, id 7676239) is 'the people' - a corporate body brought low. Operation (106, id 7676240) 'suffer sorrow'; target (107, id 7676241) 'in their affliction'. The coupling and locus carry transposed-looking values reported as recorded: coupling (112, id 7676243) holds 'internal:ib-state', locus (116, id 7676244) holds 'paired with being brought low' - the sorrow is tied to the diminishing and oppression the verse describes. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7676238) 'none'; manner (108, id 7676242) 'none'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7676245) names it: the grief of the afflicted, the low estate of the humbled - 'through oppression, evil, and sorrow'. Role (115, id 7676246) characteristic. The inner-being movement is corporate grief bound to social collapse: the people are diminished and brought low through oppression and evil, and sorrow is the interior register of that low estate. Unlike the individual laments, the bearer is a community, and the sorrow sits within a narrative that the wider psalm will reverse; here at v39 it stands as the affliction before the lifting. God is the arena whose providence the whole psalm reads behind these turns of fortune.
narratives.story: This is the sorrow of a whole people who have been beaten down. Through oppression and cruelty and trouble, they are made few and brought low, and grief is what fills them in that humbled state. It is not one person's private ache but a community's suffering, tied to their losses and their crushing. Nothing here measures it or explains it away. It stands as the low point of their story - a people diminished and grieving - within a larger song that goes on to tell how such fortunes can be turned around.

narratives.narrative: Psa 116:8 reads tears that God dries: sense (101, id 7679308) 'tears (dimah)', typed state (102, id 7679309). Bearer (105, id 7679311) is the psalmist; operation (106, id 7679312) 'weep'; target (107, id 7679313) 'then be delivered' - the weeping is read forward to its resolution. The coupling and locus carry transposed-looking values reported as recorded: coupling (112, id 7679315) holds 'internal:ib-state', locus (116, id 7679316) holds 'paired with the delivered soul' - the tears are tied to the soul God has rescued. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7679310) 'none'; manner (108, id 7679314) 'none'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7679317) names it: the weeping God turned back, grief dried by deliverance - 'you have delivered... my eyes from tears'. Role (115, id 7679318) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief in retrospect and resolved: the self looks back on tears that God has already wiped away, the eyes delivered from weeping just as the soul was delivered from death and the feet from stumbling. Here grief is neither vented nor sustained but recounted as ended - God the arena who has personally turned the tears back; the weeping is remembered from the far side of rescue.
narratives.story: Here the man looks back on tears that God has already dried. He remembers weeping, but he tells of it as something now over: God rescued his soul from death, kept his feet from stumbling, and delivered his eyes from tears. The grief is real, but it is spoken from the safe side of it - the crying has been wiped away by God's rescue. This is not sorrow in the middle of the storm but sorrow remembered with relief, the weeping stopped and the tears wiped clean because deliverance came.
narratives.variation_note: One of five readings of H1832:tear and the one that resolves. The tears are read forward to deliverance - God has turned them back, the eyes delivered from weeping as the soul was delivered from death. Contrast the unresolved Psa 42:3 (#1, tears as food) and Psa 80:5 (#3, corporate tears as bread), the treasured Psa 56:8 (#2), and the productive Psa 126:5 (#5, tears that seed joy). Here uniquely the weeping is recounted from the far side of rescue - grief already ended by God.

narratives.narrative: Psa 126:5 reads tears as seed: sense (101, id 7685133) 'tears (dimah)', typed state (102, id 7685134). Bearer (105, id 7685136) is 'the sowers' - a communal agricultural figure. Operation (106, id 7685137) 'weep'; target (107, id 7685138) 'while sowing'. The coupling and locus carry transposed-looking values reported as recorded: coupling (112, id 7685140) holds 'internal:ib-state', locus (116, id 7685141) holds 'paired with reaping in joy' - the weeping is tied to the joyful harvest it precedes. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7685135) 'none'; manner (108, id 7685139) 'none'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. Discovery (114, id 7685142) names it: the operation of grief that seeds joy - 'those who sow in tears shall reap with shouts of joy'; weeping labour is not wasted but is the very seed of the coming harvest of joy. Role (115, id 7685143) characteristic. The inner-being movement is grief made productive: tears are not an end-state but a sowing, an investment whose return is joy. Distinct from every other tears-reading, weeping here has a promised yield - the sorrow of the present labour becomes the seed of future gladness; the community are the whole-self bearer, and the arena is the reversal God works between sowing and reaping.
narratives.story: Here tears are like seed being planted. Those who go out weeping as they scatter their seed will come back singing when the harvest comes in. The grief is real - hard, sorrowful labour - but it is not wasted; it is an investment, and what it yields is joy. This is weeping with a promise attached: the sorrow of today's work becomes the seed of tomorrow's gladness. It is grief pointed forward to a harvest, the tears of sowing turning into shouts of joy at the reaping.
narratives.variation_note: One of five readings of H1832:tear and the only one where weeping is productive - tears sown as seed that yields a harvest of joy. Contrast Psa 42:3 (#1, tears as static food), Psa 56:8 (#2, tears treasured), Psa 80:5 (#3, corporate tears as bread), Psa 116:8 (#4, tears God dries). Here uniquely the grief is an investment with a promised return - sorrow forward-looking, the seed of future gladness rather than a condition endured.

narratives.narrative: Psa 126:6 reads weeping that goes out and comes home rejoicing: sense (101, id 7685155) 'weeping (bakah)', typed state (102, id 7685156). Bearer (105, id 7685158) is 'the sower'; operation (106, id 7685159) 'go out weeping'; target (107, id 7685160) 'bearing seed'. The coupling and locus carry transposed-looking values reported as recorded: coupling (112, id 7685162) holds 'internal:ib-state', locus (116, id 7685163) holds 'paired with coming home in joy' - the outgoing grief is tied to the joyful return. Source (103) present:false; seat (104, id 7685157) 'none'; manner (108, id 7685161) 'none'. Intensity (109), specifier (110), effect (111), prohibition (113) present:false. narratives.story: The picture continues: a man goes out to sow, and he goes out weeping, carrying the precious seed he is about to bury in the ground. Parting with that seed, trusting it to the soil, is felt as a real sorrow - he sets off in tears. But the grief of going out is tied to the joy of coming back: the promise is that he will return home singing, carrying armfuls of harvest. This is sorrow at the start of hard, hopeful work - weeping on the way out, joy on the way home.

narratives.story: By the rivers of Babylon, far from home, the exiles sat down and wept - and what set them weeping was remembering. The moment they thought of Zion, their lost city, the tears came. This is a whole community grieving together, not one person's private sorrow, and its trigger is memory: the sight of a foreign land bringing back everything they had lost. There is no measuring it - just displaced people whose remembering breaks into weeping. It is the ache of homesickness for a place taken from them.
narratives.variation_note: Second of two readings of H1058:wept (bakah). In Psa 69:10 (#1) the weeping is one man's devotion - weeping and fasting before God - which is then twisted into reproach. Here (Psa 137:1) the weeping is corporate exiles' grief triggered by remembering the lost Zion. The difference: 69:10 is private worship betrayed into mockery (oriented toward God); 137:1 is communal homesickness loosed by memory (oriented toward a lost place).

narratives.story: This 'grievous' is not the man's own pain but something wrong inside him that he asks God to find. He opens himself completely and invites God to search him and see whether there is any hurtful or false way in him - and if there is, to lead him out of it onto the everlasting way. It is an act of honest self-examination: rather than hiding his faults, he wants them exposed so they can be dealt with. He hands the inside of himself over to God's inspection, willing to have whatever is harmful uncovered and removed. It is grief's word turned into a request to be corrected.
